Definition: Arguing 'A or B; A; therefore not B' when the 'or' is not exclusive. Unless the options genuinely exclude each other, one being true does not rule out the other.
Example: Someone argues, 'You can have tea or coffee. You chose tea, so you cannot have coffee.'
FaithDiscussionExample: Someone argues, 'Worship can be in spirit or in truth. This service worships in spirit, so it cannot be in truth' — yet John 4:24 joins both.
HowToRespond: Check the 'or': "'Or' often means 'and/or' — could both be true together here?"
